summary: Describes a Service Selection extension for Mobile IPv4 that helps a home agent choose among several services for one subscription. This is an informational document.

plainLanguage.summary: One phone plan may include several services. This lets a traveling device say which service it wants, so the home office knows what to give it.

questions: how does a home agent select a service
how does mobile ipv4 support multiple services
what is the service selection extension
how does a home agent route based on service
subtitle: How Mobile IPv4 users can specify which service they want.

tldr.problem: A mobile node's subscription may include access to multiple services (enterprise networks, specialized domains, different routing policies), but the home agent had no way to know which service the mobile wanted.
tldr.mechanism: A new Service Selection extension (type 151) lets the mobile node include a service identifier in its Registration Request. The home agent uses this to select the appropriate routing, address allocation, firewall rules, and security policies for that service.
tldr.outcome: Operators can now offer flexible, multi-service subscriptions and apply per-service policies without requiring separate home agents.

today: RFC 5446 is an Informational Standard, providing guidance for Mobile IPv4 service selection in operator networks. A similar mechanism for Mobile IPv6 is defined in RFC 5149. These extensions are used by operators who offer multiple services within a single mobility subscription, especially in WiMAX and 3GPP2 networks.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Mobile IPv4 lets a device maintain its IP address while roaming between networks. However, identifying the mobile node alone—by home address or Network Access Identifier (NAI)—does not capture the full picture of what the mobile needs. A single subscription may grant access to multiple services:

  • Enterprise data networks hosted by the mobility provider
  • Specialized service domains not accessible from the public Internet
  • Multiple service domains separated by operator policies

Without a way to specify which service is needed, the home agent cannot apply the correct routing, address allocation, firewall, or security policies. This document specifies a Service Selection extension for Mobile IPv4 Registration Requests (and Replies), allowing the mobile node to identify the requested service.
sections.plainLanguage: The home office needs to know not just who you are, but what service you are using. This extension is how you tell it.

sections.title: Service Selection Extension Format
sections.content:
The Service Selection extension is a Mobile IPv4 skippable extension (type 151). It carries a variable-length service identifier string, 1 to 255 octets long. The identifier is encoded as UTF-8 and normalized using Unicode Normalization Form KC (NFKC), allowing international service names.

Examples of valid identifiers include 'ims' (IP Multimedia Subsystem), 'voip', and 'voip.companyxyz.example.com'. The identifier must be unique among the home agents to which the mobile node is authorized to register. At most one Service Selection extension is included in any Registration Request. When service selection is used, the extension must be included in every Registration Request.

In the Registration Request, the extension must appear after the MN-NAI extension (if present) and before any authentication-enabling extensions. In the Registration Reply, the home agent MAY echo the Service Selection extension back unchanged, using the same placement rules.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a text label like 'voip' or 'enterprise' that your device sends to the home agent. The home agent uses it to decide what service to activate.

sections.title: Processing Considerations
sections.content:
When a mobile node includes the Service Selection extension in a Registration Request, the home agent must authenticate the mobile node and verify that it is authorized to the specified service. If the mobile node is not authorized, or if the home agent does not recognize the service, the home agent denies the registration and returns a Registration Reply with error code 151 (SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED).

The Service Selection extension affects multiple home agent functions: it helps authorize the mobile, may influence Home Address allocation (the same NAI might receive different addresses for different services), may determine outbound packet routing based on service, and may trigger different quality of service treatment or security policies.

If a new Registration Request specifies a different service than the current binding, the home agent must re-authorize the mobile node. It may need to assign a different Home Address or delete the existing binding and reject the registration. The home agent MAY also apply default service selection if the extension is absent, typically plain Internet access.
sections.plainLanguage: The home agent checks: Is this person allowed to use the 'voip' service? If yes, it gives them the right addresses, routing, and security for voice calls. If no, it rejects them.

sections.title: Foreign Agent Role
sections.content:
A foreign agent (access router) MUST skip the Service Selection extension if the mobile node already included one in the Registration Request. However, if the Registration Request lacks the extension, the foreign agent MAY add it on behalf of the mobile node. How the foreign agent learns which service the mobile node needs is outside the scope of this specification—it might use link-layer signaling, provisioning, or other mechanisms.

If a foreign agent added the Service Selection extension to a Registration Request, it must check whether the home agent echoed the extension back in the Registration Reply. If the home agent included it, the foreign agent MUST NOT include it again in the Registration Reply it forwards to the mobile node, since the mobile node expects to receive the home agent's reply unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes the access router can figure out what service you need and add that information to your request. But once the home agent replies, the access router must not change it.

sections.title: Security and Authorization
sections.content:
The Service Selection extension is protected by the same authentication mechanisms as the rest of the Registration Request and Reply. It does not introduce new security mechanisms; instead, it extends the authorization phase to verify that the mobile node is authorized for the specific service identified.

The home agent MUST verify both that the mobile node is authenticated (via the standard Mobile IPv4 authentication extensions) and that it is authorized to use the selected service. Both checks must succeed before the mobile node is allowed to register. Service authorization MUST be based on the subscription data, and the authorized services list SHOULD be part of the mobile node's general subscription record.

If the service selection information is sensitive (because revealing which service a mobile uses could leak business information), it can be protected in the same way as Registration Requests and Replies, using the standard authentication extensions.
sections.plainLanguage: The request is protected with the normal security lock. The home agent checks your password and also checks that your subscription includes the service you asked for.
